Spatial Accumulation of Interaction Diversity

Source: R/network.R
spaccNetwork.Rd

Accumulate an interaction network over space: interaction richness and interaction Hill numbers, sample coverage, the richness of the two interacting levels (for example plants and pollinators) and connectance, all along the same site orders.

Usage

spaccNetwork(
  interactions,
  coords,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  n_seeds = 50L,
  method = c("knn", "nn_walk"),
  distance = c("euclidean", "haversine"),
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  progress = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  focal_points = NULL,
  focal_domain = NULL
)

Arguments

interactions

A data frame of observed interactions with columns site, lower, upper and optionally count (interaction frequency, default 1 per row). lower and upper name the species of the two levels; an interaction is a lower-upper pair.

coords

A data frame with columns x and y, one row per site. Sites in interactions are matched to coords$site if present, otherwise to the row names of coords, otherwise taken as row numbers.

q

Numeric vector. Orders of diversity. Default c(0, 1, 2).

n_seeds

Integer. Number of random starting points. Default 50.

method

Character. Accumulation method: "knn" or "nn_walk".

distance

Character. "euclidean" or "haversine".

parallel

Logical. Use parallel processing? Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer. Number of cores.

progress

Logical. Show progress? Default TRUE.

seed

Integer. Random seed.

focal_points

Optional focal points for method = "knn". See spacc().

focal_domain

Optional polygonal focal domain. See spacc().

Value

An object of class spacc_network containing:

interaction, lower, upper

Named lists (one per q) of n_seeds x n_sites matrices: Hill numbers of the interaction frequencies and of the summed frequencies of each level's species

coverage

List with the n_seeds x n_sites sample coverage matrices of interaction, lower and upper

connectance

n_seeds x n_sites matrix of interaction richness divided by the product of the two species richnesses

q, coords, n_seeds, n_sites, n_interactions, n_lower, n_upper, method, orders

Parameters, dimensions and site orders

Details

Each unique lower-upper pair is a unit of diversity and its frequency its abundance, so the interaction Hill number of order q is the ordinary Hill number of the interaction frequencies of the accumulated sites, the effective number of equally frequent interactions, and the sample coverage is the Chao & Jost (2012) coverage of those frequencies (Chiu et al. 2023). The species curves of the two levels use each species' summed interaction frequency. Connectance is the realised share of the possible interactions between the species detected so far.

References

Chiu, C.-H., Chao, A., Vogel, S., Kriegel, P. & Thorn, S. (2023). Quantifying and estimating ecological network diversity based on incomplete sampling data. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 378, 20220183. doi:10.1098/rstb.2022.0183

See also

spaccHillCoverage() for the same quantities on species

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
coords <- data.frame(x = runif(30), y = runif(30))
interactions <- data.frame(
  site = sample(30, 400, replace = TRUE),
  lower = paste0("plant", sample(12, 400, replace = TRUE)),
  upper = paste0("bee", sample(20, 400, replace = TRUE))
)
net <- spaccNetwork(interactions, coords, n_seeds = 10)
net
plot(net)
# }
